                                        PROJECT NO. 58482

                                                §       PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
  LARGE LOAD DEMAND                             §
  MANAGEMENT SERVICE                            §                    OF TEXAS

                          COMMENTS OF AEP TEXAS INC. ON
                    COMMISSION STAFF’S PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION

TO THE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS:

        AEP Texas Inc. (AEP Texas) files these comments in response to the Proposal for

Publication (PFP) of new 16 TAC §25.521 issued by the Public Utility Commission of Texas

(Commission) on July 30, 2026. The PFP set a deadline of September 4, 2026, for submission of

comments; these comments are timely filed. An Executive Summary is included at the end of the

comments.

                                   I.      INTRODUCTION
        Proposed rule §25.521 relating to Large Load Demand Management Service (LLDMS) is

the Commission’s response to the language of PURA §39.170(b), enacted by Senate Bill 6 in 2025

during the Texas 89th Regular Legislative Session, which directs the Commission to require

ERCOT to develop a reliability service to competitively procure demand reductions from large

load customers with a demand of at least 75 megawatts to be deployed in the event of an anticipated

emergency condition.

        In addition to seeking comments on the language of the proposed rule, the Commission

also invited interested persons to address 4 specific questions about the rule. AEP Texas is

providing responses to those questions. In addition, AEP Texas reiterates and incorporates the

Responses to Commission Staff Questions it filed in this Project on April 4, 2026, to the extent

those Responses address issues that remain relevant to the proposed rule as published.



Project No. 58482                                                            AEP Texas’s Comments
                                                                                        Page 1 of 8
                       II.     RESPONSES TO SPECIFIC QUESTIONS

1.      Proposed subsection (f)(1)(C) authorizes payment to a qualified scheduling entity
        representing a large load customer that is not instructed by ERCOT to deploy but is
        subject to availability verification during the Large Load Demand Management
        Service (LLDMS) obligation period. Should a large load customer that is available
        but not ultimately instructed to deploy during the LLDMS obligation period be
        compensated some percentage of the market clearing price for the large load
        customer’s availability to reduce demand during the LLDMS obligation period? If
        so, what is an appropriate payment to the large load customer for their availability
        during the LLDMS obligation period?

        AEP Texas does not support making payments to large load customers unless they are

instructed to deploy. LLDMS should not function as a broad demand response service but as a

focused tool for ERCOT to use to deal with extreme emergency issues involving system reliability.

As ERCOT studies weather conditions and transmission system emergencies, its determination of

where load reduction is needed will evolve and it may ultimately need less participation in a

procurement than was originally thought. Unless it is determined over time that the obligation

period imposes much more severe inconvenience or cost to large loads not deployed than

anticipated, there is no need to impose unnecessary cost on the market for demand reduction that

is not necessary in addressing an emergency condition. The potential for local load reductions to

address geographically limited problems makes it unlikely that the same large load customers will

be repeatedly asked to be available; thus, no incentive other than payment for deploying should be

necessary to get them to participate.


2.      Proposed subsection (f)(4) imposes a maximum budget of $54 million in a calendar
        year. What is an appropriate budget for the LLDMS program?

        AEP Texas takes no position on the maximum budget amount but does recommend that


Project No. 58482                                                            AEP Texas’s Comments
                                                                                        Page 2 of 8
 whatever number is selected function as a cap or a ceiling, not as a target. ERCOT should engage

in rigorous analysis to ensure that payments are not made simply because the dollars are available,

and payments should not be made in circumstances where large loads are reasonably expected to

reduce voluntarily. When an emergency event is developing, ERCOT should analyze the issues

and identify a necessary procurement amount. Then demand reduction payments should be limited

to amounts necessary to return ERCOT to normal operations. In each emergency instance, the

total LLDMS payment should be structured and limited to the event, based on the best information

at the time, not simply a target spend limit.


3.      What cadence should ERCOT use to assess an extreme weather condition and how
        far in advance should ERCOT start the auction to procure LLDMS?

        ERCOT should have the discretion to make this determination based on the kind of extreme

condition it anticipates, the state of the market at the time, the experience it has over time with the

effectiveness of the LLDMS service, the analysis it can perform at the time of the occurrence, and

the urgency associated with the condition. LLDMS should be utilized as a service deployable on

a localized basis; ERCOT’s knowledge of the available load in the area should be one of several

factors ERCOT must consider before deciding how much to pay for LLDMS and when action

should be taken to procure the demand reductions it anticipates being required. Defining a cadence

for ERCOT and a time period within which it must act imposes unreasonable requirements on use

of a service that may not need to be deployed often and risks spending more than necessary on

demand response payments, to the detriment of all ERCOT customers.


4.      Should ERCOT be allowed to deploy LLDMS for transmission emergencies? If so,
        what limitations, if any, should the Commission impose on this authority?

        LLDMS is a service that could work well to address transmission emergencies, and the



Project No. 58482                                                                AEP Texas’s Comments
                                                                                            Page 3 of 8
 Commission has authority under the language in PURA §39.170 to allow ERCOT to employ it for

that purpose. No special limitations should be imposed on ERCOT’s use of this authority,

particularly because ERCOT should learn over time how LLDMS functions in real time situations

and whether and how effectively it addresses grid issues. ERCOT should have the discretion to

assess anticipated emergency conditions like those occurring on the transmission grid and to

analyze how best to address them to return the grid to normal operations.


                    III.   RECOMMENDATIONS BY RULE SUBSECTION

A.      The Directive to ERCOT in section (a)(1) that transmission and distribution utilities,
        electric cooperatives and municipally owned utilities be required to develop
        equipment or technology to curtail large loads during firm load shed may be
        inconsistent with current operational capabilities.

        Many transmission providers may have limited ability to remotely disconnect large load

customers short of opening the main breaker at the site. Such action would disconnect the entire

load, which may not be the action ordered by ERCOT during an LLDMS deployment. Earlier

commenters have suggested that a SCED-based centralized approach administered by ERCOT and

installation of SCED-integrated load curtailment is the better solution to achieving curtailment

under the proposed rule. However, it is unknown whether this is a manageable solution in a

reasonable time frame. Because section (a)(2) of the rule provides that ERCOT must develop

LLDMS consistent with “this section”, presumably referring to section (a)(1), ERCOT’s ability to

proceed with LLDMS soon may be limited.

        AEP Texas suggested in its comments filed on April 8, 2026, in this project that a directive

implementing PURA §39.170(a) be included in the proposed rule. Consistent with that but

recognizing that there may be technical barriers to complying with the directive, AEP Texas

suggests that the language in section (a)(1) be modified to address such technical issues, as follows:

Project No. 58482                                                               AEP Texas’s Comments
                                                                                           Page 4 of 8
         §25.521. Large Load Demand Management Service (LLDMS).
        (a)     Directive to ERCOT.
                (1)    To the extent compliance with this directive is technically feasible,
                       ERCOT must ensure that each electric cooperative, transmission and
                       distribution utility, and municipally owned utility serving a
                       transmission-voltage customer develops a protocol, including the
                       installation of any necessary equipment or technology before the
                       customer is interconnected, to allow the load to be curtailed during firm
                       load shed.


B.      The rule should be clarified to confirm that LLDMS can be used to address
        transmission emergencies.

        As indicated in these comments, AEP Texas supports the application of LLDMS to address

emergency conditions on the ERCOT transmission grid. In fact, there may be situations where the

curtailment of one large load customer could address a transmission issue, demonstrating the value

of the localized function of LLDMS service under the proposed rule. Although “transmission

emergency” is defined in the rule, it does not appear in the sections of the rule referring to LLDMS

procurement or deployment. AEP Texas recommends that the term “emergency condition” found

in PURA §39.170(b) be added to the definitions in the rule to confirm that transmission conditions

are included in the emergency conditions for which LLDMS is being created. In addition, the

defined term “transmission emergency” should be included in rule provisions regarding

procurement, as follows:


        §25.521. Large Load Demand Management Service (LLDMS).

        (b)     Definitions.
                (5)    Emergency Condition -- Conditions for which LLDMS may be
                       procured such as Transmission Emergency and Extreme Weather
                       Conditions.

Project No. 58482                                                             AEP Texas’s Comments
                                                                                         Page 5 of 8
         (d)     Procurement. ERCOT may procure LLDMS from a large load customer on an
                as needed basis to help prevent an anticipated EEA event due to an extreme
                weather condition, or to alleviate an actual EEA event due to an extreme
                weather condition., or to address a transmission emergency.
                (1)    Request for proposal. ERCOT may issue a request for proposal to large
                       load customers that are pre-qualified to participate in LLDMS:
                       (C)     in advance of an anticipated EEA Level 1 event due to an
                               extreme weather condition or to address a transmission
                               emergency; or
                       (D)     during an EEA event due to an extreme weather condition or to
                               address a transmission emergency.
        (e)     Deployment.
                (2)    ERCOT may deploy a large load customer as necessary to help maintain
                       reliability during an EEA event due to an extreme weather condition or
                       to address a transmission emergency throughout the LLDFMS
                       obligation period.


C.      Language should be added to section (c) requiring ERCOT to make available to
        transmission service providers any list it develops of pre-qualified Large Loads.

        As AEP Texas suggested in its earlier comments in this project, the rule should include

language regarding how and when the list of participating customers will be provided to each

applicable transmission and distribution utility in its implementation of PURA §39.170(b). AEP

Texas recommends that the following language be added to section (c) of the rule:


        §25.521. Large Load Demand Management Service (LLDMS).

        (c)     Participation. Participation in LLDMS is limited to large load customers that
                pre-qualify for participation at least annually. ERCOT shall provide the list to
                each applicable transmission and distribution utility as soon as possible after
                each list is finalized.




Project No. 58482                                                             AEP Texas’s Comments
                                                                                         Page 6 of 8
 D.      Section (f)(1)(C) authorizing payment to large load customers who are subject to
        availability verification by ERCOT during the LLDMS obligation period but are not
        instructed to deploy should be deleted.

        For the reasons detailed above in response to question 4, payment to large loads that are

not instructed to be deployed should not be authorized as part of LLDMS. Section (f)(1)(C) should

be deleted in its entirety. If the Commission elects to retain the language, the Commission should

instruct ERCOT to provide, with each such payment, the justification for doing so. Payments

under this provision should be an exceptional form of relief, not an expectation.

                            IV.     CONCLUSION AND PRAYER
        AEP Texas appreciates the opportunity to provide these comments concerning

recommended changes to proposed rule 16 TAC §25.521.

              EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF AEP TEXAS INC.’S COMMENTS
                  REGARDING PROPOSED RULE AS PUBLISHED

•     AEP Texas does not support making payments to large load customers unless they are
      instructed to deploy.

•     AEP Texas takes no position on the maximum budget amount but does recommend that
      whatever number is selected function as a cap or a ceiling, not as a target. The total LLDMS
      payment should be carefully structured and limited to the event, based on the best
      information at the time, not simply a target amount to be spent.

•     Defining a cadence for ERCOT and a time period within which it must act to request bids
      for LLDMS procurement imposes unreasonable requirements on use of a service that may
      not need to be deployed often and risks spending more than necessary on demand response
      payments, to the detriment of all ERCOT customers. ERCOT should use its discretion and
      learn about the service as it is utilized.

•     LLDMS is a service that may be effective in addressing transmission emergencies, and the
      Commission has authority under PURA § 39.170 to allow ERCOT to employ it for that
      purpose.

•     The directive to ERCOT in § 25.521(a)(1) that transmission service providers be required to
      develop equipment or technology to curtail large loads during firm load shed may be
      inconsistent with current operational capabilities. The rule should be modified to provide
      flexibility for transmission service providers when technical barriers exist to load
      curtailment.

•     The rule should be clarified to confirm that LLDMS can be used to address transmission
      emergencies. “Emergency Conditions”, as used in PURA § 39.170, should be added to the
      definitions in the proposed rule and “Transmission emergency”, as defined in the rule, should
      be inserted in several rule provisions.

•     Language should be added to subsection (c) requiring ERCOT to make available to
      transmission service providers any list it develops of pre-qualified Large Loads.

•     Subsection (f)(1)(C) authorizing payment to large load customers who are subject to
      availability verification by ERCOT during the LLDMS obligation period but are not
      instructed to deploy should be deleted.
